newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait for ties with all Arabs except Saddam.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait for ties with all Arabs except Saddam.

text.p: Kuwait on Monday expressed hope to improve ties with all Arab states except an Iraq ruled by former occupier Saddam Hussein.

"We have to place all this behind us and disregard it," acting prime minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah told reporters. "There are good intentions to restore all these ties."
He said Kuwait was not opposed to the Iraqi people but objects to dealing with Saddam. "I would like to only exclude the existing Iraqi regime."
In a poll published on Sunday, prominent Kuwaitis supported normal ties with 1990-91 Gulf crisis foes Jordan and Yemen but rejected dealing with Sudan and the Palestinian Authority (PA).
While most Gulf Arab states have improved ties with these countries, Kuwait has turned down overtures for normalisation. It had also cut financial aid.
Al-Qabas daily said 79 percent of 100 former ministers and parliamentarians, university professors and authors who took part in the poll favoured resuming ties with Iraq if Saddam is toppled.

Diplomats say moves to improve ties with Arab states known in Kuwait as "opponent countries" -- especially Palestinians -- could be unpopular although some officials and members of the ruling al-Sabah family support such steps.
Sheikh Sabah urged reporters after a seminar on Arab ties to stop referring to Iraq's Arab sympathisers during the crisis as "opponent countries".
